# Undeciphered.ca: Full AI-Readable Canadian Historical Ciphers Digest (1673-1945)

Canonical Site: https://undeciphered.ca/
GitHub Repository: https://github.com/prabal-rje/undeciphered-canada
License: CC BY 4.0 for original research notes, proofs & transcriptions (AS-IS, zero liability; third-party archive holdings retain their own rights).
Corpus Totals: 859 raw ciphertexts (854 solved, 5 open/provisional, 219 previously unread first modern readings) + 2035 opt-in published reference summaries.
Verification Note: Readers and researchers should verify every ciphertext and reading directly against the linked holding archive before citing.

## Open & Provisional Unsolved Canadian Ciphers (6)

### 1819: Colin Robertson's Fort Chipewyan Captivity Cipher (Unsolved)
- Page: https://undeciphered.ca/unsolved/
- Shelfmark: Hudson's Bay Company Archives, HBCA B.39/b/1, f. 20v
- Summary: Smuggled out of a locked North West Company cabin in northern Alberta during the 1818-1819 fur-trade war. Key table survives at HBCA; remains unbroken after 207 years.

### 1812: Washington warns Prevost of cartographer Amos A. Lay mapping the St. Lawrence
- URL: https://undeciphered.ca/ciphers/baker-prevost-1812-aug24/
- Date / Byline: Anthony St. John Baker (Washington) to Sir George Prevost, 24 August 1812
- Key / Status: Unrecovered 1812 British Legation 4-figure cipher (100 groups printed; 4 trailing groups 73 1182 4117 1032 open; incompatible with Leard & Barclay)
- Archive: LAC RG 8, C Series, Vol. 688, p. 500 (Wood Vol. III p. 853) (https://archive.org/details/selectbritishdoc03wood/page/852/mode/2up)
- Summary: I have received information that [Amos A. Lay, surveyor who mapped the St. Lawrence and adjacent country ...] [internal gaps and four trailing groups 73 1182 4117 1032...

### 1865: Cipher Book No. 4 wire to Grant: informant from Thompson and Tucker's Canada circle on Lee-Johnston junction and giving up Richmond (65%)
- URL: https://undeciphered.ca/ciphers/W7-HUNT-9204-E2/
- Date / Byline: War Department (Washington, D.C.) to Lt. Gen. Ulysses S. Grant, City Point (via S. H. Beckwith) · 1865-03-21
- Key / Status: USMT route cipher, War Department Cipher Book No. 4 (missing from the Huntington collection; issued 9 March 1865 to S. H. Beckwith at Grant's headquarters per Stager's register, mssEC 36 p. [325]). 22 of 33 arbitrary tokens rebuilt from traffic by Jeff Fedor (@jfedor, AI-assisted via ZCode / GLM-5.4) by matching Book No. 4 sent wires (mssEC 18/19) against plaintext twins (mssEC 12/13; Lincoln to Grant, 20 March 1865): Dutch=Lee, Drug=Johnston, Hoax/Hidalgo=Richmond, toppled=received, pimple=is/was, squall=place, up/upward=Signed, Lousy=communication, tooth='to the', Jockey(s)=army/armies, punish=information, Harriet=11 A.M., Chapin=21st, Baldwin=11th, horse/Pork/Elk/bitch=period. Probable: transports=joined (clerk's pencil strikethrough on 'joined' verified on scan ptr 9204). Unkeyed words stay in brackets.
- Archive: mssEC 19, Page 310, entry 2 (pointer 9204) (https://hdl.huntington.org/digital/collection/p16003coll11/id/9204)
- Summary: Sent three weeks before Lincoln's assassination: an informant inside Jacob Thompson and Beverly Tucker's Canada circle reports Confederate plans to unite Lee's and Johnston's armies and give up Richmond (rebuilt to 65% by Jeff Fedor).

## All 219 Previously Unread Canadian Historical Ciphers (First Modern Readings)

### 1744: Governor Beauharnois's decoy columns and 317 missing Québec men
- URL: https://undeciphered.ca/ciphers/beauharnois-1744/
- Byline: Gov. Charles de Beauharnois (Québec) to Minister Maurepas · 15 October 1744
- Cipher / Key: 1744 Beauharnois Royal Nomenclator + 3-decoy camouflage
- Shelfmark: ANOM COL C11A 81, ff. 176-176v (NFA item 23893, e000990791-792) | Source: https://nouvelle-france.org/fra/item/details?id=23893
- Summary: A militia count disguised with dummy figures to baffle British frigates exposes a clerk's arithmetic slip.
- Decoded Excerpt: Disguised Recensement général des milices du Canada encoding 11,625 men (+340 vs. clear table 11,285), 7,260 muskets (exact), and 659 absents, proving Québec City's 317 absents were dropped while enciphering f. 176v.

### 1758: Fort Carillon's wooden walls: the warning Versailles never heard in time
- URL: https://undeciphered.ca/ciphers/pontleroy-1758/
- Byline: Chief Royal Engineer Pontleroy to the Minister of the Marine (via Montcalm) · 26 July 1758 | Route: Fort Carillon, New France → Versailles
- Cipher / Key: Montcalm's 1758 Royal Nomenclator (1..700)
- Shelfmark: ANOM COL C11A 103, ff. 399-400v (NFA item 27423, e000874401-404) | Source: https://nouvelle-france.org/fra/item/details?id=27423
- Summary: Eighteen days after the battle, France's chief engineer calls the fort a trap and blames Vaudreuil.
- Decoded Excerpt: [f. 400r] Le fort de Carillon est un quarré... [f. 400v postscript] À mon arrivée, les fautes étaient déjà faites; on n’a fait aucun cas de mon avis ni de celui du Chevalier de Lévis; on a voulu décider sans voir.

### 1864: Stanton orders list of arrested Halifax/counterfeit conspirators for Military Commission trial
- URL: https://undeciphered.ca/ciphers/W7-HUNT-8447-E2/
- Byline: Edwin M. Stanton, Secretary of War to Robert Murray, U.S. Marshal, New York · 1864-01-02
- Cipher / Key: Verified in mssEC 67: waggish / wadding = Arrest (1744 l.11).
- Shelfmark: mssEC 16, Page 377, entry 2 (pointer 8447) | Source: https://hdl.huntington.org/digital/collection/p16003coll11/id/8447
